lifecycles._note: Light read-only lifecycle: covers the two collection GETs that 2xx with no resource. GET /v1/vpn-gateways (listvpngateways) and GET /v1/vpn-tunnels (listvpntunnels) both return 200 on an empty account — confirmed live 2026-06-29. The id-bound GETs (showvpngateway, showvpntunnel) need real ids; none exist in the account (ledger: 0 gateways/tunnels, 404 not 403 with fake ids). This lifecycle targets only the safely reachable collection endpoints. No teardown required (read-only). Ceiling for this lifecycle: 2/10. All 6 write ops + id-bound shows remain in the heavy lifecycle (networking-vpn-gateway-tunnel). Region gate: VPN only in kr-west1/kr-east1/kr-south3; the collection GETs are still safe to call on other regions (empty list 200).

REPAIR 2026-07-06 (HB4 400 ValidationError ["Field required"], run 28738115294, OFFLINE repair — see CAMPAIGN-C3-100-repair-log.md #HB4b): create-vpn-gateway was missing the REQUIRED `ip_address` field. `data/api_docs.json` models['networking/vpn/vpngatewaycreaterequest'] lists `ip_address` as required:true (string) alongside ip_id/ip_type/name/vpc_id — the create body only carried ip_id/ip_type/name/tags/vpc_id, so the backend's generic 'Field required' 400 (no field name in the error body) is now attributable to the missing `ip_address`. Fix: create-publicip now also captures `$.publicip.ip_address` (per `networking/vpc/createpublicip` response_example: publicip.ip_address is a real routable IP, e.g. "192.167.0.5") into `publicip_ip_address`, and create-vpn-gateway's body sends `ip_address: {publicip_ip_address}` — the gateway's own IP is the address of the public IP it's attached to (ip_id), consistent with the model's paired ip_id/ip_address/ip_type triple. UNVERIFIED LIVE (offline repair, no SCP calls this session) — next heavy dispatch (HB4c or similar) must confirm 2xx. VPN gateway + tunnel CRUD (Wave 2, NOT runtime-proven, HEAVY/billable). A VPN gateway needs a base VPC + a public IP. The VPC is the session-shared VPC (adopt:vpc, per knowledge/vpc-scheduling-strategy.md — does NOT self-create a VPC); a publicip is created on the vpc service for the gateway's ip_id. Then: create-gateway -> get/set-gateway, create-tunnel -> get/set-tunnel, delete-tunnel, delete-gateway. gateway+tunnel writes are one optional 'vpn' group so a bad body / missing publicip skips only this family (cleaned up children-first). Bodies from data/api_docs.json request_example. create-gateway returns $.vpn_gateway.id, create-tunnel returns $.vpn_tunnel.id (both soft-captured; dependent steps reference {vpn_gateway_id}/{vpn_tunnel_id} -> real chain on success, literal-but-norm-matching on 4xx so coverage still records). gateway needs vpc_id + ip_id(public ip) + ip_type:PUBLIC + ip_address; tunnel needs vpn_gateway_id + phase1/phase2 crypto blocks (enum lists from docs, UNVALIDATED). The phase1/phase2 DH-group + encryption values are the OFFICIAL doc request_example combo ([30,31,32] + des-md5/chacha20poly1305-prfsha256 / null-md5/aes128gcm/chacha20poly1305; replaced the earlier [14]/aes256-sha256 guesses 2026-07-04, see docs/working/plans/CAMPAIGN-C3-100-docs-research.md #4) — still UNVALIDATED live, so optional/4xx-tolerant; perfect_forward_secrecy ENABLE|DISABLE is a confirmed enum. USERGUIDE FACTS VERIFIED/APPLIED 2026-06-11 (knowledge/formal/services/networking__vpn.yaml, pending live validation): gateway/tunnel names must be 3-20 chars, LETTERS+DIGITS ONLY (no hyphens/underscores) — regrvpngw{ualpha} (17 alnum) and regrvpntun{ualpha} (18 alnum) comply, do NOT reintroduce 'regr-' hyphenated names; the gateway create REQUIRES a Public IP (ip_id) + connected VPC — both already encoded (publicip created on the vpc service before the gateway); the tunnel requires the gateway (encoded chain) with PSK 8-64 chars (ours: 17), max 10 remote-subnet CIDRs (ours: 1), DPD interval 1-3600s (ours: 60); teardown order tunnels-then-gateway and gateway not deletable while Creating/Editing (encoded via 409-retries). REGION GATE: VPN exists ONLY in kr-west1/kr-east1/kr-south3 (not south1/2) — the engine has NO region-guard mechanism yet, so the gate lives in this note (declarative 'regions' key = future work); default env stage-kr-west1 is in-gate. Covers all 6 VPN WRITE ops: POST /v1/vpn-gateways, PUT /v1/vpn-gateways/{vpn_gateway_id}, DELETE /v1/vpn-gateways/{vpn_gateway_id}, POST /v1/vpn-tunnels, PUT /v1/vpn-tunnels/{vpn_tunnel_id}, DELETE /v1/vpn-tunnels/{vpn_tunnel_id}.

steps.name: list-igw-for-vpn
steps._note: REPAIR 2026-07-07 (HB4c, run 28833316852, OFFLINE repair — see CAMPAIGN-C3-100-repair-log.md §HB4c item 2): adopt-or-create bootstrap, added because create-igw-for-static-nat in networking__loadbalancer.json (same shared VPC) 400'd `already-associated` in this SAME run — CONFIRMED at most ONE IGW per VPC (the error body names the existing one), and both this lifecycle and the LB one adopt the single session-shared VPC without self-creating one, so whichever family's create fires SECOND now collides. List existing IGWs on `{vpc_id}` first (`networking/vpc/listinternetgateways`, response_example wraps as `internet_gateways[]`); if one already exists (created by the LB family, or a prior run) capture its id into `igw_id` so wait/set/create-vpn-gateway proceed against a real IGW either way. If none exists yet this finds nothing and the following create-igw-for-vpn step makes one. See that step's own note for why the DELETE step must NOT reuse this adopted `igw_id`.

steps.name: create-igw-for-vpn

json.description: API regression IGW for VPN gateway

steps._note: REPAIR 2026-07-07 (HB4b-2, run 28827996068, OFFLINE repair — see CAMPAIGN-C3-100-repair-log.md #HB4b-2 item 1): create-vpn-gateway 404s `scp-network.vpn-gateway.internet-gateway-not-found` ("Cannot found the Internet Gateway on VPC(...)") — CONFIRMED from the observation's own error body, not a guess. Pattern lifted verbatim from the proven networking__loadbalancer.json create-igw-for-static-nat fix (same live error class, itself lifted from networking__vpc.json's create-internet-gateway-for-nat, CONFIRMED live 2026-06-23) — create IGW on the same (session-shared) VPC, wait ACTIVE, PUT/set it, THEN create-vpn-gateway. CONFLICT CHECK (per task instruction — this lifecycle ADOPTS the shared VPC, does not self-create one, so a concurrently-scheduled heavy lifecycle could try to attach a 2nd IGW to the same VPC at the same time): `data/api_docs.json` has no documented 1-IGW-per-VPC cardinality limit, and TWO other lifecycles already create/attach an IGW on this same shared VPC as an established, previously-proven pattern (networking__vpc.json create-internet-gateway-for-nat, live-CONFIRMED 2026-06-23; networking__loadbalancer.json create-igw-for-static-nat, HB4b OFFLINE repair). UPDATE 2026-07-07 (HB4c): this WAS observed as a genuine collision in run 28833316852 — the LB lifecycle's create-igw-for-static-nat 400'd `already-associated` while this lifecycle ran concurrently. Rather than switching to a self-created VPC (VPC-budget cap-5 waste for zero coverage benefit), added the `list-igw-for-vpn` adopt-or-create bootstrap above so a 400 here (this family running second) is a non-event — `igw_id` was already resolved to the other family's IGW by the list step. `owned_igw_id` is captured ONLY here (from OUR OWN create response), separately from the adoption-tolerant `igw_id`, so the cleanup dict above and the explicit `delete-igw-for-vpn` teardown step below key off `owned_igw_id` — if this create 400s (adopted, not owned), `owned_igw_id` stays unset and both those DELETE calls hit an unresolved literal path (safe 404), NEVER the other family's real IGW. UNVERIFIED LIVE (offline repair) — next heavy dispatch must confirm 2xx AND that a concurrent run with the LB static-nat family no longer 400s on either side's create.

steps.name: delete-igw-for-vpn
steps._note: REPAIR 2026-07-07 (HB4c, run 28833316852, OFFLINE repair — see CAMPAIGN-C3-100-repair-log.md §HB4c item 2): path changed from `{igw_id}` to `{owned_igw_id}` — `igw_id` may now be an ADOPTED IGW (see list-igw-for-vpn's note) belonging to a concurrently-running lifecycle (e.g. networking__loadbalancer.json's LB static-nat family), and this suite must never delete another family's live resource. `owned_igw_id` is captured only by create-igw-for-vpn's own 2xx and stays unset when we adopted instead of created, so an adopted case leaves this DELETE targeting an unresolved literal path (safe 404, matches this codebase's established soft-capture-miss convention) instead of the foreign IGW. Delete the IGW created for the VPN gateway, children-first (after delete-vpn-gateway, before delete-publicip/delete-vpc). Retry 400 to ride out the not-deletable-state transition (same quirk CONFIRMED for this endpoint in networking__vpc.json / mirrored in networking__loadbalancer.json's delete-igw-for-static-nat).
